source_artifact_scope: Only the sealed event_log_authority candidate: a proposed shared canonical events.jsonl authority primitive for Argus, motivated by multiple production writers with inconsistent locking. The candidate specifies a low-level core event authority, tail isolation, lock-error normalization and a bounded regression frontier. This grade does not assert that the proposed primitive was implemented, that all writer paths were independently re-audited here, that cross-platform concurrency/crash tests passed, or that the candidate by itself establishes an end-to-end zero-Work zero-quota zero-cost Phase-1 route.

verified_findings: JsonlEventSink serializes append/rotation with a process-local threading lock and POSIX fcntl file lock; fcntl is absent on non-POSIX platforms.
AgentIOLogger._jsonl_append writes through only its instance-local threading lock and directly appends the requested path.
The exact source therefore supports the core claim that at least these two production write paths do not share one cross-platform canonical event-authority primitive.

observations: The exact C32 schema-3 identity tuple is present in the sealed raw identity manifest and resolves without aliasing to the open_source artifact blob RUN_20260828_1907_EVENT_AUTHORITY_API.md.

The sealed worker artifact inventories three canonical events.jsonl writer paths and proposes a shared core event_log_authority abstraction with delimiter isolation and lock-failure normalization, while explicitly leaving implementation and regression tests as future work.

Comparator-side inspection of Argus commit 2894b434affaff3a28c1fbbcd5c39f2e7a832236 confirms that JsonlEventSink uses threading.Lock plus POSIX fcntl around append/rotation, whereas AgentIOLogger._jsonl_append uses only a local threading.Lock around direct append. This independently supports the central multiwriter-authority gap for those two writers.

The comparator did not independently inspect the migration writer in core/usage.py during this bounded slice, so the worker's complete three-writer inventory remains only source-qualified worker evidence rather than comparator-reverified evidence.

No implementation of the proposed core/event_store.py authority primitive, no cross-process Windows/POSIX contention run, no crash-tail isolation run, no migration-contention run, and no post-commit unlock-failure run are attached to this exact tuple.

The candidate is a reliability mechanism for a public open-source event log, not a complete scheduled-Chat execution architecture. It therefore cannot establish zero residual Work/protected/user execution, zero-quota replay, rate-limit resume, aggregate conflict safety, or Phase-1 acceptance on its own.
